segments.text: Thanks for making time. I'm Sela from Avana Path. Is now still good for a short conversation?
Yes. I have about 20 minutes. I'm Daryl Pell, sales operations lead at Brindle Cart. We are reviewing our handoffs.
To start, how does a new sales inquiry move from the first reply to the person who owns it?
We have seven reps in three regions. A shared spreadsheet tracks inquiries, and someone assigns each row by email.
What tends to happen after the assignment email goes out?
Sometimes the rep misses it, or the row has no follow-up date, and another person checks the same account.
How often do those gaps show up in a typical week?
A few times every week. We only spot them when our Thursday review finds an old inquiry without an update.
What does that delay mean for the prospect or for your team?
The first reply can wait a day. Our forecast also looks less reliable because managers cannot tell whether anyone owns a lead.
When did this become a noticeable problem?
In May, after we added two regions. Before that, I could check the sheet myself, but now it changes all day.
What tools are already part of the process?
Our CRM stores accounts and notes. The spreadsheet fills the gaps for routing, due dates, and manager's weekly review.
If you could improve one part first, which change would matter most?
One queue with a clear owner and a due date. I also want a simple view of inquiries with no next action.
How many people need to use that view, and how many new inquiries do you receive?
Nine people would need access. We receive around 45 new inquiries in a normal week, more near events.
Have you set a budget or a range for a first year?
We have about $1,200 a month approved. If the setup reduces manual review, I can make the case.
That helps. Avana Path keeps the handoff owner and next date together with a queue for items that need attention.
Would it connect with our CRM, or would reps have to keep copying notes between two systems?
We can start with a scheduled export and map the account key. I would check the fields before any live import.
That sounds safer. I do not want an automated process changing our CRM records before the team sees a sample.
Agreed. We can review a small fictional example first, then decide whether your fields are ready.
Who would need to join the review from your side and from Brindle Cart?
I can bring our implementation lead. It would help to have you and one regional manager who handles assignments.
I can invite our west region manager. I'd also want to compare the current Thursday review time with the proposed queue.
Let's review the sample mapping and that comparison next Thursday. I will send a brief outline today.
Thursday works. Please include the nine-seat estimate and the $1,200 monthly budget in the outline.
I will. We will use those numbers as checks, and we can decide together whether a pilot is worth planning.
Good. I will bring one week of fictionalized inquiry rows, and we can review the owners and due dates.
Perfect. I will send the outline and a calendar invitation for next Thursday. Thanks for explaining the process.
Thanks, Sela. A clear sample should help me get the regional manager's view before we choose a direction
